title: Labeled-quant (TMT/iTRAQ) pipeline support
context: Many large-scale cancer proteomics studies (e.g., CPTAC-style analyses) use isobaric labeling (TMT, iTRAQ) for quantification rather than label-free DDA or DIA approaches. Supporting labeled quantification extends the project's coverage to a significant fraction of public cancer proteomics datasets. The pipeline must follow the same reproducibility standard: pinned containers (immutable digests), complete run manifests, FDR validation, and 100%-provenance CI gate. Methods review is expected to be heavy given the additional complexity of reporter-ion deconvolution and normalization.
objective: Implement a containerized labeled-quantification (TMT/iTRAQ) pipeline extension that meets the same reproducibility standard as the DDA and DIA pipelines, validated on an approved open labeled-quant dataset.
acceptanceCriteria: A containerized TMT/iTRAQ pipeline extension is implemented within the Nextflow workflow, with pinned tool versions (e.g., FragPipe with TMT-Integrator or equivalent) referenced by immutable container digest.
The pipeline runs on an approved open labeled-quant dataset (passed allow-list gate: open-access, de-identified, license verified, re-id determined).
FDR-controlled identifications and normalized reporter-ion quantities are validated by the FDR/statistics harness.
A complete run manifest is produced; 100% of published assertions pass the CI provenance gate.
Pipeline code is MIT-licensed; aggregate tables are CC-BY-4.0; commit is DCO signed-off; pnpm build && pnpm test && pnpm lint pass.
output: A committed PR containing the containerized TMT/iTRAQ pipeline extension, validated on an approved open labeled-quant dataset with complete run manifest and passing CI; code MIT, tables CC-BY-4.0.
